result.topic_en: Riemann works out limiting cases of the modular functions: he reduces the transformation formulas for log k, log k' and related quantities to Dedekind-type sums $((\mu t/n - 1/2))$ and transforms these sums.
result.transcription:
Grenzfälle der Modulfunctionen. Ueberführung der Ded.[?] formel in die Riemann'sche[?]
$m\mu \equiv 1$ mod $2n$
[-$\frac{m+n}{2}\mu \equiv ...$-]
[-$\frac{m+n}{2}\mu \equiv n+1$ mod $2n$-]
$\frac{m+n}{2}\mu \equiv \frac{n+1}{2}$ mod $n$
I 3. $\lg\frac{2k}{\pi} = \frac{\pi i}{3n}\{(m,n) - 2(\frac{m+n}{2}, 2n)\}$
$= 2\pi i \sum ((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12))\{((\frac{t}{n}-\frac12)) - 2((\frac{\frac{m+n}{2}\mu t}{n}-\frac12))\}$
$= 2\pi i \sum ((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12))\{((\frac{t}{n}-\frac12)) - 2((\frac{n+1}{2n}t-\frac12))\}$
$= 2\pi i \sum ((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12))\{((\frac{t}{n}-\frac12)) - 2((\frac{t}{2n}+\frac{t}{2}-\frac12))$
$t \equiv 0$ mod 2. $((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12))$ $t<n$
$t \equiv 1$ mod 2 $((\frac{t}{2n}))$
$\frac{t}{n}-\frac12 - 2(\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12)$. $t \equiv 0$ $\frac12 + (-1)^t\frac12$[?]
$\frac{t}{n}-\frac12 - \frac{t}{2n}$[?] $t \equiv 1$
$= \pi i \sum_{1,n-1}(-1)^t((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12))$ bei Riemann. $2\pi i\sum_{1,n-1}(-1)^t((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12))$
Leider stimmt überein[?] dem:
$((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12)) = 2((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12)) \pm \frac12$ $\pm$ $((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12)) \lessgtr 0$
$((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12))$ u. $((\frac{\mu(n-t)}{2n}-\frac12)) = -((\frac{\mu t}{2n}))$ haben gleiches Zeichen, und $(-1)^t, (-1)^{n-t}$ entgegengesetztes. folglich $\sum((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12)) = 2\sum((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12))$

III 3 [-$\frac{\lg\theta}{\pi i}$-] $\lg\frac{2k}{\pi} = \frac{\pi i}{3n}((m,n) - (m+n, 2n))$
$= 2\pi i(\sum_{1,2n-1}((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12))((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12)) - 2\sum_{1,4n-1}((\frac{t}{4n}-\frac12))((\frac{(m+2n)t}{4n}-\frac12))$
$= 2\pi i \sum_{1,2n-1}((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12))((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12)) - 4\sum_{1,2n-1}((\frac{\mu t}{4n}-\frac12))((\frac{t}{4n}+\frac{t-1}{2}))$
$((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12)) = 2((\frac{\mu t}{4n}-\frac12)) \pm \frac12$ $\pm$ $((\frac{\mu t}{4n}-\frac12))$
$= 4\pi i \sum_{1,2n-1}((\frac{\mu t}{4n}-\frac12))\{\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12 - \frac{2t}{4n}+1$ $t$ gerade[?]
$-\frac{t}{4n}$ $t$ ungerade
$= 2\pi i\sum(-1)^t((\frac{\mu t}{4n}-\frac12))$
$\pm \pi i\sum\pm(\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12) = 0$ weil die Glieder mit $t$ und $2n-t$ sich aufheben.

I. 2. $\lg k' = \frac{\pi i}{3n}\{2(\frac{m+n}{2}, n) - (m, 2n)\} = 4\pi i\sum_{1,n-1}((\frac{t}{n}-\frac12))((\frac{(m+n)t}{2n}-\frac12)) - \sum_{1,2n-1}((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12))((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12))$
$m\mu \equiv 1$ mod $2n$
$= 4\pi i(\sum_{1,n-1}((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12))((\frac{t}{2n}+\frac{t-1}{2})) - 2\sum_{1,n-1}((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12))((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12))$ $((\frac{\mu t}{n}-\frac12)) = 2((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12)) \pm \frac12$
$= 8\pi i\sum_{1,n-1}((\frac{\mu t}{2n}-\frac12))\{((\frac{t}{2n}+\frac{t-1}{2})) - ((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac12))\} =$ [-$8$-] $4\pi i\sum_{1,n-1}((\frac{\mu \tau}{2n}-\frac12))$ $\tau$ ungerade
$= -4\pi i\sum_{1,n-1}((\frac{\mu(n-\tau)}{2n}))$ $n-\tau = 2t$ gerade. $\lessgtr^{n-1}_{0}$ $[\alpha]$ kleinste ganze Zahl[?]
$= -4\pi i\sum_{1,\frac{n-1}{2}}((\frac{\mu t}{n}))$; nun ist allgemein $\alpha = \mathcal{E}(\alpha) + [\alpha]$ $((\alpha - \frac12)) = [\alpha] - \frac12$
$\alpha = \mathcal{E}(\alpha) + ((\alpha-\frac12)) + \frac12$ $((\alpha)) = \alpha - \mathcal{E}(\alpha+\frac12)$
also.
$= -4\pi i\{\sum\frac{\mu t}{n} - \sum_{1,\frac{n-1}{2}}\mathcal{E}(\frac{\mu t}{n}+\frac12)\} = -\pi i\{\frac{n^2-1}{2n}\mu - 4\,\mathcal{E}(\frac{\mu t}{n}+\frac12)\}$ Wie bei R.

methods.what: Transformation of log(2k/π) expressed via Dedekind-type sums (case I 3)
Reduction of case I 3 to an alternating sawtooth sum
Relation between sawtooth values at μt/n and μt/(2n)
Symmetry t ↔ n−t giving equality of sums
Case III 3 reduced to alternating sum over 4n

methods.what: Case I 2: log k' reduced to sawtooth sum and then to floor-function sum
Identities relating sawtooth function to integer part
